ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: After a certain student learned the knowledge of celestial motion, he imagined that there exists in the universe an isolated star system composed of four stars. As shown in the figure, one parent star is at the center of an equilateral triangle, and at each vertex of the triangle there is a small star of equal mass moving in circular motion around the parent star. If the universal gravitational force between two small stars is F, and the universal gravitational force between the parent star and any one small star is 9F, then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The universal gravitational force received by each small star is $(\sqrt{3}+9)F$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a dashed equilateral triangle, and at each of the three vertices a small circle is drawn to represent three small stars; at the central position inside the triangle a small circle is drawn to represent the parent star. Choose the small star at any one vertex for analysis. Then reason: This small star is subject to the universal gravitational forces of the other two vertex small stars, both with magnitude F. Because the three vertices form an equilateral triangle, the angle between these two forces is 60°. The magnitude of the resultant of the two forces is R=√(F^2+F^2+2F·F·cos60°)=√3F, and the direction is along the angle bisector of that vertex pointing toward the center of the triangle. The magnitude of the universal gravitational force of the parent star on this small star is 9F, and the direction is also along the same straight line pointing toward the center. Therefore the magnitude of the resultant universal gravitational force received by each small star is √3F+9F=(√3+9)F.
